subject: the selected Arrange track header's context menu as a coordinate-free exact-reorder provider
question: Does the selected track header expose a semantic command that moves that exact track before or after another retained track?

reverify.command: With a disposable flat project stopped, retain the selected Arrange header and full physical order; right-click only that already-selected header, recursively census the resulting owned menu without pressing a leaf, invoke Cancel on that exact menu object, then reread order, selection, routing, focus and transport.
reverify.expected: The complete menu contains reassignment, creation, naming, deletion, stack, visibility, color, icon and header-configuration commands but no before/after, up/down or exact-position track move; exact-menu cancellation leaves the retained state unchanged.
reverify.cost: needs Logic 12.3 with a disposable flat project open; read-only menu census; about one minute

method: The protected flat fixture was first read with no menu open: 32 headers, one retained header selected, transport stopped and not recording, and the selected strip routed to its retained physical output. The already-selected header was opened by its context-click surface. Every AXMenu and descendant item already exposed under that owned root was read; no item was pressed. The exact root menu's exposed cancellation accessibility action dismissed it. A fresh full AX read then compared order, selection, routing, focus, transport and menu absence. No global keyboard input, drag, save or project mutation was used.

observations.what: representative semantic branches present in the menu

rows.meaning: reassign the selected track to an existing object

observations.what: state after cancelling the exact owned menu

canon_not_applicable.reason: The conclusion is about runtime AX structure, complete menu membership and before/after state, not the wording of any menu title. Exact observed titles are retained only in the attached raw census.

conclusion: The selected header's complete context menu contains 102 items across 11 menu containers, but zero item provides an anchor-relative, up/down or exact-position track move. Reassignment targets existing objects and stack creation changes hierarchy; neither is an exact retained-track reorder primitive. Together with the existing key-command census and the retained header's lack of a reorder action or writable position, this closes the last measured coordinate-free provider candidate on this host. Exact L2 arbitrary reordering is platform-limited here and must refuse rather than simulate a drag.
limits: One Logic build, one locale, one flat 32-header fixture and one already-selected audio track.
This proves absence from the recursively exposed selected-header context menu on this host; it does not prove that no future Logic build or private protocol can expose an exact reorder provider.
The Mixer strip context menu was not opened. It is lower-value because Mixer reordering can create or move Arrange tracks and still lacks a retained before/after anchor contract.
No menu leaf was pressed, so this record does not qualify reassignment, stack creation, coloring, naming or any other listed command.
This settles the bounded L2 provider investigation only. It does not complete #969's grouping, view-layout or broader live-integration acceptance.
